title: The bot team
summary: A bench of AI assistants, each with one job. A chief-of-staff assistant hands work to the others: drafts, edits, research, code, the inbox, the calendar, notes.
detail: They can prepare all day. They do not send, post, or spend. That waits for me.

title: Social pipeline
summary: The bots draft a week of posts and line them up. Every Tuesday I keep the ones that sound like me and kill the rest.
detail: If I don't get to the queue, it sits. Nothing publishes on its own.

title: LifeDash
summary: A board for the TV next to my desk. Three columns: personal, the work, and what I'm building.
detail: No chatbot, no database, and nothing to click. I built it to be ignored until I glance up.

title: OwnerMathSheets
summary: Spreadsheet templates for people who run the place: a plate-cost calculator, a bakery pricing sheet, and a weekly food-cost tracker.
detail: The formulas are the product. If a cell can't be explained out loud, it doesn't stay.

title: The 7:15 brief
summary: A weekday morning note. It pulls the calendar, the inbox items that matter, open loops, and whether the bots are quiet.
detail: It lands in the notes I already keep, before I start. One page, then I go to work.

title: j0sh.wtf
summary: My hub for AI tools, minus the hype. Hand-written HTML on Cloudflare Workers, no framework.
detail: On Oct 27, 2026 it scored 100 on all four Lighthouse mobile categories. The case studies live there, including the bot team.
result: Static, and fast on a phone.

title: Dad Can't Draw
summary: A company I built and sold. It isn't running, so there's no link.
